Verdict

No confirmed malicious supply-chain compromise indicators were found. Overall risk: **info**.

Malicious Supply-Chain Indicators

No confirmed malicious supply-chain indicators.

Automatic Execution Paths

  • pyproject.toml uses the hatchling.build backend. No evidence of install-time or interpreter-start execution via setup.py, .pth, sitecustomize.py, or usercustomize.py was identified.
  • project.scripts defines smoke-optimiser = "smoke_optimiser.__main__:main", which is a normal CLI entry point requiring user execution.
  • project.entry-points."pytest11" defines smoke_optimiser = "smoke_optimiser.plugin", which is auto-loaded by pytest. The observed code adds pytest options and, only when --smoke is used, reads a local .smoke_suite.json and filters tests. No malicious automatic execution behavior was identified.

Theft / Exfiltration / Persistence / Lateral Movement / Obfuscation

  • No evidence of broad credential harvesting from environment variables, .env files, SSH keys, cloud credentials, or CI/CD tokens was identified.
  • No HTTP upload, webhook, suspicious C2 domain, raw IP endpoint, or paste/drop-service exfiltration code was identified.
  • No archive staging via tar/zip/gzip/base64 or stealth loader behavior was identified.
  • No persistence mechanisms such as cron, systemd, launch agents, or shell profile modification were identified.
  • No evidence of Kubernetes, Docker socket, cloud metadata, GitHub Actions token theft, or workflow-injection lateral movement was identified.
  • The subprocess.run usage appears tied to expected user-triggered tool functionality: invoking pytest, coverage, git rev-parse, and macOS sysctl. This does not appear to be supply-chain malware behavior.

Distribution Integrity Anomalies

  • .github/workflows/*.yml and .gitignore are present in the sdist, but such project metadata/CI files are common in source distributions and do not by themselves indicate a malicious payload.
  • No suspicious native binaries, hidden executable payloads, typosquatting evidence, or sudden malicious dependency insertion were identified in the provided content.
  • GITHUB_TOKEN usage in release.yml appears consistent with release-please/checkout and Trusted Publishing workflows, with no evidence of token exfiltration.

Additional Verification Needed

  • The corpus is based on selected files, and one file is truncated near the end. Full verification of the remaining files and complete sdist contents would be needed for exhaustive review.
  • No wheel artifact was provided, so sdist/wheel mismatch could not be assessed.
  • The PyPI sdist was not compared against the remote GitHub repository source in the provided input.
